name: Dropkiller
description: Subscription platform for e-comm entrepreneurs (esp. LatAm): product insights, ad creatives, market analysis. Founded Oct 2024, US. ~10k estimated users. Note: Stripe API key on TrustMRR expired Aug 2026 — figures below are the last verified sync, not live Oct data.

mentions.evidence: ~$60,179 MRR (snapshot at last sync), 2,702 active subscriptions, ~$49,511 L30 (as of sync window), ~$452,343 all-time. Last synced ~22:22 Warsaw 15 Aug 2026 (stale Stripe key on TrustMRR).
mentions.indieAngle: Niche market-intel SaaS for one region's e-comm operators — language + payment rails as moat.

whyItPrints: Dropshippers and DTC brands pay monthly for winning-product dashboards. High seat count, checkout + recurring mix.
whyThisMatters:
Dropshippers and DTC brands in Latin America pay for a dashboard that shows which products and ads are working. Dropkiller is that research layer. Product insights, ad creatives, market analysis, and a Chrome extension so you can inspect a product without leaving the store or ad library you already have open.

The homepage is in Spanish. Creators and e-com educators in the region endorse it. They talk about a large catalog of products and millions of ads. The workflow is find a winner, spy the creative, and move into your own store faster.

TrustMRR still marks the money Stripe-verified, but the connected key expired in August 2026. The numbers you see are the last sync from that window, not a live October pull. Seat count was high then, which fits a monthly research subscription with a big free-to-paid funnel.

You pay for the radar. Language and local payment rails are part of the moat. The product is market intel for one region's operators, not another global AI toy.
